name: Timber House
blurb: A cottage grown a storey: six beds for families who can buy cloth and reach a tavern and a shrine.

name: Townhouse
blurb: Stone below, timber above, eight beds, on medium-density land. Its families want furniture, remedies, a market hall and a bathhouse.

name: Manor
blurb: A gentry house on Castle Hill. Wine, books, a theatre and a library keep it.

name: Tenement
blurb: Twelve beds stacked under one roof outside the walls. Cheap, crowded and rowdy.

name: Tall House
blurb: Four and five storeys of stone and timber built wall to wall with its neighbours: fourteen beds on a cottage's ground. Only on high-density land.

name: Root Farm
blurb: Turnips, onions and parsnips: a smaller harvest than wheat, but they keep in the clamp and feed the town through winter.

name: Barley and Hop Yard
blurb: Barley and hop poles, malted and brewed on the farm into ale for the taverns.

name: Orchard
blurb: Apple and pear trees: little in spring, a great crop of fruit and cider in autumn.

name: Quarry
blurb: Cuts stone for townhouses, walls and the great works.

name: Sheepfold
blurb: Sheep for wool and mutton.

name: Weaver
blurb: Spins and weaves wool into the cloth every timber house wants.

name: Carpenter
blurb: Chairs, beds and chests for the townhouses.

name: Herb Garden
blurb: Healing herbs for the apothecaries.

name: Apothecary
blurb: Brews herbs into remedies and tonics.

name: Fishery
blurb: Nets and smokehouses on the river bank. Feeds a city without more fields.

name: Vineyard
blurb: Wine for the manors and the high tables.

name: Scriptorium
blurb: Rag paper and patient copyists. Books for the gentry and the scholars.

name: Inn
blurb: Beds for travellers and adventurers. Newcomers stay to look the town over; heroes without a room camp, then ride on.

name: Bathhouse
blurb: Hot water and gossip. Townhouse families will not live without one.

name: Theatre
blurb: Players, plays and the talk of the season.

name: Long Nave
blurb: A longer nave for the temple: room for hundreds more at prayer.

name: Bell Tower
blurb: Bells to call the faithful. The god is pleased, and the Hollow Choir hate the sound.

name: Almshouse
blurb: Bread and a bed for the poor. Every household rests easier, and the Quiet Hand lose desperate recruits.

name: Crypt
blurb: Hallowed vaults for the town's dead, where nothing rises. The Dawn Wardens approve; the Hollow Choir seethe.

name: Cloister
blurb: A quiet garden walk and a scriptorium. Scholars of the Unshut Book come to read.

name: Great Spire
blurb: A spire seen for miles. Settlers come to see it; the Thornward Circle call it a stone thorn in the sky.

name: Watch House
blurb: A post for the watch. Each one makes every watchman count a quarter more against crime and raiders.

name: Drill Yard
blurb: Trains and quarters foot soldiers: swordsmen, spearmen and the special foot your allies and institutions teach.

name: Archery Range
blurb: Butts and a long field. Trains archers, crossbowmen and slingers.

name: Stables
blurb: Horses, fodder and a paddock. Trains outriders, knights and anything else that is ridden.

name: Watchtower
blurb:
Sees the wilds around it live, farther as the town grows.
One per 100 residents.

name: Builders' Yard
blurb: A yard of carpenters and masons. Three more homes, shops or works can go up at once, and its builders work the sites on the town's wage.

name: Granary
blurb: The town's grain store. The caravans leave more food in town, so a bad week or a raid on the farms hurts less.

name: Market Hall
blurb: A roofed market where every trade sells. Townhouse families want one near, and sales tax rises a little.

name: Courthouse
blurb: Magistrates and a lock-up. The watch counts for more, and the townsfolk trust the law.

name: Library
blurb: Chained books and quiet halls. Manors want one, and it will house the town's scholars.

name: Barracks
blurb: The city guard's hall, apart from the watch. Makes the walls a quarter stronger, and trains and quarters 60 foot soldiers.

name: Cathedral
blurb: A cathedral to the town's god in the Temple Ward. It serves the whole city and lifts every heart.

name: Arena
blurb: Games and tourneys. Heroes of renown come to fight in it, and the crowds love the mayor who pays.

name: Keep
blurb: A stone tower for the town's lord: small to begin with, and a castle once you add to it. The last wall in any siege.

name: Curtain Wall
blurb: A ring of stone round the keep's yard. The walls hold a tenth longer.

name: Castle Chapel
blurb: Where the lord's household prays before a fight.

name: Castle Gatehouse
blurb: Twin towers and a portcullis. The Dawn Wardens drill in its yard.

name: Great Hall
blurb: Feasts and audiences. The merchants of the Gilded Scale like a lord who hosts; the Quiet Hand like being watched less.

name: Barracks Wing
blurb: Bunks and an armoury for the lord's men-at-arms, and a bed for one more hero.

name: High Tower
blurb: A lookout over the whole country. The Compass Lodge borrow it to chart the hills.

name: Hall Bell Tower
blurb: A bell to call the moot. The townsfolk hear their council.

name: Council Chamber
blurb: A proper chamber for the council, with benches for the guilds.

name: Counting House
blurb: Clerks and strongboxes. The treasury takes a little more of every sale, and the Quiet Hand find less to skim.

name: Hall Archive
blurb: Deeds, charters and the watch's ledgers. The watch knows who's who; the Unshut Book come to copy.

name: Banner Court
blurb: A paved court hung with the banners of every company that rode for the town. Settlers take note.

name: Bastion Keep
blurb: A company's own hall: beds for its members, a steward and a cook from town.

name: Company Smithy
blurb: Two hired smiths make tools for the market and, each week, better arms for one of the company.

name: Physic Garden
blurb: Herb beds and a still. Each week the gardeners brew healing draughts for the company.

name: Drill Yard
blurb: Townsfolk hired as the company's sentries. They drill each week and stand on the walls in a siege.

name: Map Room
blurb: A cartographer sifts travellers' tales and old charts for places the town has never heard of.

name: Company Sanctum
blurb: A chapel of the company's own. Its acolytes tend the company's wounds and feed the town's hungry.

name: Counting House
blurb: Factors trade the company's hoard along the river roads; the town taxes what they make.

name: Proving Ground
blurb: A drillmaster runs the company through its paces between delves, so they come home sharper.

name: Hall of Banners
blurb: The company's trophies hang here. Heralds ride out with its name, and heroes ride in to join.

name: Warded Vault
blurb: Where the company keeps what it should not. Now and then something in it wakes and proves useful.

name: Adventurers' Hall
blurb: Where companies register, read the contract board, gear up and keep a sending stone of their own. Contract fees, better answers to parties who send word from the road, and a Hallmaster with requests of their own.

name: Monastery
blurb: A walled cloister round a courtyard and its falling water, with an infirmary and a herb garden. Calmer streets, fewer townsfolk who break, and monks who take to the road as heroes.

name: Griffon Roost
blurb: A timber tower of perches and nesting ledges for a flight of griffons and their riders. Safer roads, a watch from the sky, and a Roostmaster who answers to no one on the ground.

name: Harbour
blurb: A stone quay, a slipway and net sheds. Its boats fish when moored and sail trade runs down the coast; corsairs know the way in too.

name: Sky Dock
blurb: A tall timber mooring mast and a cradle of scaffolds where the town's airship is built, patched and filled. It carries one company at a time straight over rivers, lakes and mountains, out to its job and home again.

name: Fey Market
blurb: A square of lantern posts and empty stalls that fill with fey traders on moonlit nights. A happier town, stranger bargains, and a Market Warden who keeps the fey to their word.

name: Monster Sanctuary
blurb: Walled pens, deep pools and an iron aviary for wounded and orphaned monsters. Visitors, remedies or guardians, and a Beastwarden who loves every one of them.

name: Auction House
blurb: A grand, gloomy hall where relics from ruins and dead adventurers' estates go under the hammer. Excellent prices, the occasional curse, and an Auctioneer who never touches the lots.

name: Oracle's Observatory
blurb: A domed tower of brass and glass where an oracle reads stars, smoke and bones. Forewarning, calmer hearts and the gods' notice, and an Oracle who is right more often than is comfortable.

name: The Delve
blurb: A winch, a shaft and a ledger over a buried hall of the giant kings. Companies, salvage and renown come up it, and a Delvemaster who has pulled more heroes out of holes than anyone living.

name: Embassy Quarter
blurb: Envoys' houses round a fountain square: a dwarven hall half underground, a pavilion of living trees, a flooded courtyard. Wider trade roads, visitors, and a Chamberlain who keeps the peace between them.

name: Gatehouse of Ways
blurb: A ring of black standing stones that opens on places no road reaches. Rich trade, strange visitors and the odd incident, and a Warden of Ways who decides which door stands open.

name: Hall of Heroes
blurb: A long hall of trophies, memorial stones and recovered relics, with an empty pedestal by the door. More heroes stay, the town remembers its dead, and a Curator who knows every story.

name: Dragon's Eyrie
blurb: A broad stone tower on a hill, with a ledge big enough for a dragon, where a dragon lives by treaty. A guarded sky, a demanding neighbour and a great deal of meat.

name: Undercity Gate
blurb: A warded stone gatehouse over the way down into the cellars and everything under them. Whatever stirs below stirs slower, and its Gatewarden decides what goes down and what comes up.

name: Paladin Chapterhouse
blurb: A fortified hall for an order of paladins. A little more safety, an oath that shapes the town, and a Knight-Commander who expects the town to keep its word.

name: Alchemists' Quarter
blurb: A lane of stills, kilns and coloured smoke. More potions and herbs, a little gold, and a Master Alchemist whose accidents are the town's problem.

name: Artificers' Foundry
blurb: Furnaces, lathes and a great water-wheel. Better tools, faster building, and a Forgemaster whose inventions have minds of their own.

name: Druid Grove
blurb: A patch of living wilderness: an ancient tree, a sacred pool and its druids. Richer fields, healing herbs, and a Grove Warden with opinions.

name: Grand Bazaar
blurb: A caravanserai and covered market for far-travelled merchants. One more trade route, exotic goods, and a Bazaar Warden who knows every road.

name: Clock Tower
blurb: A grand work: a tall clock tower over the green. Market days keep time, traders trust the hour, and the bells give the town a voice.

name: Aqueduct
blurb: A grand work: arches carry clean hill water into the town's fountains. Every household is better content, and word of sweet water draws settlers.

name: Great Gatehouse
blurb: A grand work: a fortress gate of twin towers, a portcullis and murder holes. The walls hold far longer, and the watch commands every road in.

name: Mage Tower
blurb: A grand work: a tower of warded stone for the wizards of the marches. Spellcasters and adventurers seek out a town that has one, so more heroes make it their home.

name: Royal Gardens
blurb: A grand work: terraced gardens, an orangery and fountains open to all. The whole city takes its ease there, the mayor is loved for it, and visitors write home about it.

name: Colossus
blurb: A grand work: a bronze-and-stone colossus of the town's founder, its lantern seen for a day's ride. Pilgrims and traders come to see it, and the mayor who raised it is remembered.

name: Lofted Spire
blurb: The Lofted City, small: one Skywright spire on a keelstone. Machinery first, then the halls, then it rises. Heroes, settlers, Mandate and lore; it can sail.

name: Sky Isle
blurb: The Lofted City, middling: an isle of streets and towers on three keelstones. Machinery first, then the city, then it rises. A great boost to heroes, settlers, trade, Mandate and lore; it can sail.

name: Lofted City

stages.name: the high city and its palace

blurb: The Lofted City, whole: a city on five keelstones, with a harbour for airships and a palace in the clouds. Machinery first, then the city, then it rises. The greatest boost a town can build; it can sail.

name: Great Cathedral
blurb: A wonder of the great city: a cathedral whose spire is the tallest thing in the realm, raised over a generation. Every household is prouder for it, and the council stands behind a mayor who gave the town its heart.

name: Royal Palace
blurb: A wonder of the great city: a palace fit for a crown the town has not yet been offered. Envoys, merchant princes and famous heroes come to be seen at its court.

name: Skyward Citadel
blurb: A wonder of the great city: a citadel of towers on the town's highest ground, crowned by a beacon that burns all night. Whatever comes against the walls, the citadel's garrison and its wards stand behind them.
